title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
This page begins the second half of the memoir, the dynamics of strings. The 'second general problem' asks for principles that determine the motion of a perfectly flexible or elastic thread, acted on at every point by arbitrary forces. The motion is assumed to stay in the plane of the thread's figure.

In the solution (§XXXV) Euler first sets up the kinematics, before any forces are introduced. He says this keeps the number of quantities small at the outset.

Setup:
- Fix an initial epoch. At time t (measured in seconds) the thread occupies the curve AMB, referred to a fixed axis AD or a line parallel to it.
- The endpoint A may itself move. So A can no longer be the fixed origin of abscissas.
- The arc AM = s is measured from the material end A. Because the thread is inextensible, s is in effect a material (Lagrangian) label for the particle M.
- The tangent MT makes the angle XMT = φ with the coordinate direction.

The key observation is that φ can no longer be a function of s alone. The same material arc s has different tangent angles at different times, so φ = φ(s,t). The study therefore belongs to 'that quasi-new part of Analysis' dealing with functions of two variables, the partial differential calculus.

The next page completes the kinematics:
- (∂x/∂s) = sin φ and (∂y/∂s) = cos φ, so x = ∫ds sin φ and y = ∫ds cos φ, with s alone varying in the integrals.
- The velocities are (∂x/∂t) and (∂y/∂t); the accelerations are (∂²x/∂t²) and (∂²y/∂t²).
- Multiplying by the element's mass Σ(s)ds and dividing by 2g (Euler's unit convention) gives the forces needed to sustain the supposed motion.

In modern terms this is the material, intrinsic-angle formulation of the planar dynamics of an inextensible string or elastica. The inextensibility constraint |∂r/∂s| = 1 is built in by parametrising the tangent through φ.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; it is purely set-up and definitions.

Calling the analysis of functions of two variables 'quasi novam' is rhetorical. Euler had used partial differentiation since the 1730s and had written on PDEs for the vibrating string (E119, E140) and in Inst. calc. integralis vol. III (1770).

ideas.what: Use arc length from a material endpoint as a Lagrangian label for an inextensible moving string, with the endpoint itself free to move
ideas.modern_name: Material (Lagrangian) coordinates / intrinsic description of an inextensible rod
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (Truesdell's 1960 history of flexible and elastic bodies discusses E410 explicitly)
ideas.where_published: E410 itself (Novi Comm. Petrop. 15, 1771); compare E481 and earlier string papers

ideas.what: Tangent angle φ treated as a function of two variables φ(s,t), with partial derivatives (dφ/ds), (dφ/dt)
ideas.modern_name: Intrinsic angle formulation; partial derivatives / PDE for string dynamics
ideas.where_published: E119, E140, Institutiones calculi integralis III

ideas.what: Separate the kinematics from the forces: first compute the 'required forces' (mass × acceleration), then equate them to the applied and internal forces
ideas.modern_name: Effective-force / d'Alembertian formulation of Newton's second law for continua
ideas.where_published: E177 Découverte d'un nouveau principe de mécanique

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard set-up of the material/intrinsic kinematics for string dynamics. It is already well covered in Truesdell's history of E410; nothing new.
